requirement:
`languages::PlainText` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims no extensions. The filename-based constructors
select it when no supplied language claims the extension, including filenames
without an extension, under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
The structural check finds no gap. I did not independently assess runtime behavior or test adequacy.

**`OutlineLang` implementation.** The `language!` invocation for `PlainText` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/languages/mod.rs` carries the `{impl}` reference. It expands to `impl super::OutlineLang for PlainText`. That impl supplies the three methods `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider` calls for:
- `name()` returns `$profile.name`.
- `extensions()` returns `$profile.extensions`.
- `outline(&self, &str) -> Result<Outline, OutlineError>` calls `parse_with(&PROFILE, source)` and converts the result with `Outline::from_legacy`.

**Default value, cloning and extensions.**
- The macro declares `pub struct PlainText;` as a unit struct with `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]`. It therefore has a default value, and cloning copies no configuration, so it is cheap.
- `PlainText` uses `super::plain::PROFILE`, defined in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/plain.rs` with `name: "plain-text"`, `extensions: &[]` and `language: None`. It claims no extensions.

**Fallback selection.**
- `OutlineContent::from_source` first asks `languages::registry().for_path(filename)`. When no registered provider claims the path, it falls through to `Self::from_source_with(&languages::PlainText, ...)`.
- `OutlineContent::from_path` delegates to `from_source`.
- A filename without an extension, or with an unclaimed one, therefore gets `PlainText`. This sits under `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`, which already has its own `{impl}` reference on `from_source`.

I also saw tests that appear to check these points. They are `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`, which asserts the name `plain-text` and empty extensions, and `profiles_are_selected_by_extension_case_insensitively` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs`, which maps `notes` and `notes.rs.txt` to plain text.

text: :::{req} language
`languages::PlainText` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims no extensions. The filename-based constructors
select it when no supplied language claims the extension, including filenames
without an extension, under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
:::{req} language_provider
`OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Stable name of this language implementation.
fn name(&self) -> &str;
/// Claimed filename extensions, without their leading dots.
fn extensions(&self) -> &[&str];
/// Interpret supplied text into selectable items and structural hashes.
fn outline(&self, source: &str) -> Result<Outline, OutlineError>;
:::{req} defaults
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
The [language chapters](#language-specific-rules) define those mappings.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
[plain-text outline](sources/plain-text.md): a file root with one child per
nonblank line.
